title: Who Pays and Splitting the Bill
short: Traditionally whoever invites pays; with friends, agree before ordering whether to split evenly or pay for what you ordered.
trouble: Learners split evenly after one person ordered far less, or argue at the table. Customs vary, so settle it early and cheerfully.

blocks.html: At the end of a restaurant meal comes the bill. Money can make good friends awkward, and a little planning prevents almost all of it.
Traditionally, whoever invites pays. With friends, agree before ordering whether you will split the bill evenly or each pay for what you ordered. Then follow the plan cheerfully.

Clear expectations protect friendships. The person who says "Let me take you to dinner" has offered a gift, so they pay. Among friends, an even split is simple when orders are similar, but unfair when one person ordered much less. Settling it early means nobody orders under a cloud of worry, and nobody argues over a receipt.

blocks.title: An uneven table
blocks.q: Four friends go out. Three order meals around \$28. Omar orders only soup for \$9. The bill comes. What is fair?
steps: An even split would make Omar pay for food others ate.
It is fairer for each to pay for what they ordered, plus a share of tax and tip.
Even better: agree on this before ordering.
blocks.a: Each pays for their own order, or the friends agree that Omar pays less.

blocks.title: Even shares
blocks.q: Five friends agree to split a \$90 bill evenly, tip already included. How much does each pay?
steps: Divide the total by the number of people: \$90 ÷ 5.
